title: Validity of a machine configuration encoding
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$, and assign a Boolean value $a$ to each bit of the encoding, whose bits represent input positions, an input-head position, a state, work-tape cells, and a summary. The assignment is valid when exactly one input-head position and exactly one state are selected; on each work tape exactly one of the $2s+1$ positions is selected; at each work-tape position the two bits indexed by $0$ and $1$ are not both true; and the two summary bits are not both true.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet
A Boolean assignment to the encoding bits
